page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-80 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 80 virtual CPUs across 40 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It delivers 80 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware graphics accelerators, relying exclusively on attached persistent storage solutions for persistence.

Performance profiles demonstrate strong multi-threaded execution capabilities. In benchmark testing, the instance scored in the top 25 percent for stress-ng multi-core tests (107,952.86) and PassMark overall CPU computation (69,646.99). Hardware cryptographic instruction support, including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, yields top-decile execution in PassMark CPU encryption tests (85,363.22). Software build benchmarks such as Clang compilation (43,413.0) and ray tracing tasks (70,957.0) also perform in the upper quartile. Cached memory throughput reaches 5,077.68 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth achieves 109.12 GB/sec. Conversely, raw Geekbench multi-core and single-core scores fall within the middle 50 percent of cloud instances.

The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio establishes high computational density without allocating surplus memory overhead, optimizing cost efficiency for compute-dominated environments. However, the absence of local NVMe storage and the constrained memory footprint make it unsuited for large in-memory databases or caching layers with high capacity demands. The platform is well suited for CPU-bound batch processing, continuous integration compilation pipelines, mathematical simulation workloads, video rendering, and multi-threaded cryptography services.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-80 is a compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 80 vCPUs across 40 physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with a lean 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, it offers 80 GB of system RAM without bundled local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration. Benchmark measurements highlight upper-quartile results in multi-core compute tests, Clang compilation, and ray tracing, backed by top-decile encryption processing through hardware AES and SHA acceleration. Cached memory bandwidth delivers 5,077.68 GB/sec, while large-block write operations register at 109.12 GB/sec. The instance delivers high processing density for CPU-heavy tasks without excess memory spend, though it requires network storage for persistent disk access. This architecture makes the instance suited for compilation pipelines, distributed microservices, rendering tasks, cryptography workloads, and multi-threaded batch compute jobs.
